paper.title: Stochastic Linear Optimization under Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear optimization under bandit feedback (compact decision set D in R^n)
unmapped: Noise is a martingale difference sequence: E(c_t(x)|H_t) = mu.x for all histories, costs in [-1,1] (not necessarily i.i.d.)
Learner has access to a barycentric spanner of D
Mean costs mu.x in [-1,1] on D (losses, minimisation)
settings.definition_quote: Let D ⊂ R^n be a compact (but otherwise arbitrary) set of decisions. Without loss of generality, assume this set is of full rank. On each round, we must choose a decision x_t ∈ D. Each such choice results in a cost ℓ_t = c_t(x_t) ∈ [−1, 1]. We assume that, regardless of the history H_t, the conditional expectation of c_t is a fixed linear function, i.e., for all x ∈ D, E(c_t(x) | H_t) = μ · x ∈ [−1, 1].

settings.name_in_paper: Lower-bound instance: D_n = (S^1)^{n/2}, product of circles, {-1,+1} costs, mu uniform on D_n/n
unmapped: Decision set is a Cartesian product of n/2 unit circles (gap Delta = 0)
Costs take values in {-1,+1} with mean mu.x
settings.definition_quote: Assume n is even. Let D_n = (S^1)^{n/2} be the Cartesian product of n/2 circles... Our cost functions take values in {−1, +1}, and for every x ∈ D_n, the expected cost is µ · x, where nµ ∈ D_n.

bound.regime: Delta > 0; holds simultaneously for all T with probability >= 1-delta

source.quote: Suppose the decision set D and the true mean µ have a gap ∆ > 0. ConfidenceBall2: For all sufficiently large T, the cumulative regret R_T of ConfidenceBall2(D,δ) is with high probability at most O(n^2/∆ log^3 T). More precisely, Prob(∀T, R_T ≤ 8nβ_T ln(T)/∆) ≥ 1 − δ

results.notes: Paper's n is dimension d; Delta is the extremal-point gap. Regret R_T = sum of mu.x_t - mu.x* (random). CB2 may be NP-hard on polytopes.

extra_assumptions: ConfidenceBall1 implemented to choose only extremal points

source.quote: ConfidenceBall1: If ConfidenceBall1 is implemented so that it only chooses extremal points x_t ∈ D (which is always possible) then ... with high probability at most O(n^3/∆ log^3 T). More precisely, Prob(∀T, R_T ≤ 8n^2β_T ln(T)/∆) ≥ 1 − δ

results.notes: Polynomial time given a linear optimization oracle over D (O(n) oracle calls per round).

source.quote: ConfidenceBall2: For all sufficiently large T, the cumulative regret R_T of ConfidenceBall2(D,δ) is with high probability at most O*(n√T) ... More precisely, Prob(∀T, R_T ≤ √(8nTβ_T ln T)) ≥ 1 − δ.

results.notes: O*(n sqrt T); holds also when Delta = 0.

source.quote: ConfidenceBall1: For all sufficiently large T, the cumulative regret R_T of ConfidenceBall1(D,δ) is with high probability at most O*(n^{3/2}√T) ... More precisely, Prob(∀T, R_T ≤ √(8n^2Tβ_T ln T)) ≥ 1 − δ.

results.notes: O*(n^{3/2} sqrt T); efficient given linear optimization oracle.

source.quote: If µ is chosen uniformly at random from the set D_n/n, and the cost for each x ∈ D_n is in {−1, +1} with mean µ · x, then, for every algorithm, for every T ≥ 1, E R = E_µ E(R | µ) ≥ (1/10) n√T.

results.notes: Bayesian lower bound on a fixed instance family with Delta = 0 (product of circles); implies minimax lower bound. Proof sketch for general n only states Omega(sqrt T) per component.
